oahu: an island of central Hawaii (between Molokai and Kauai); the chief island of the state
oak: the hard durable wood of any oak; used especially for furniture and flooring
a deciduous tree of the genus Quercus; has acorns and lobed leaves
great oaks grow from little acorns

oar: an implement used to propel or steer a boat

oas: an association including most countries in the western hemisphere; created in 1948 to promote military and economic and social and cultural cooperation
oasis: a fertile tract in a desert (where the water table approaches the surface)
a shelter serving as a place of safety or sanctuary

seed of the annual grass Avena sativa (spoken of primarily in the plural as `oats')
oatcake: thin flat unleavened cake of baked oatmeal
oates: English conspirator who claimed that there was a Jesuit plot to assassinate Charles II (1649-1705)
oath: profane or obscene expression usually of surprise or anger
a commitment to tell the truth (especially in a court of law); to lie under oath is to become subject to prosecution for perjury

oatmeal: meal made from rolled or ground oats

oaken: consisting of or made of wood of the oak tree
